history.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Draw a new instructional mechanism diagram background from scratch. Reference images are external instructional references only, for scientific separation of stages and visual objects; do not reproduce their layouts or text. Design the composition yourself. Use genuinely transparent surrounding canvas (later placed on pure white), crisp flat 2D shapes, ample negative space, thin dark gray connectors, sparse clearly separated semantic groups. Use Lancet semantic hues: blue #7B95C6/cyan #49C2D9 for records, green #67A583 for observation/environment, peach #FFC1A6/rose #C85E62 for construction and optimization, yellow #FDED95 for learned outputs and evaluation. Use pale uniform opaque fills mixed with white inside some groups and plain white in others. Exactly uniform continuous color areas, NO gradients, NO paper/canvas textures, NO noise, NO ripples, NO stripes, NO cloudlike tone variation, NO shadows/gloss, NO decorative 3D/perspective/extruded surfaces. Mechanism objects should be recognizable 2D records, stacks of flat sheets, branching samples, operator groups, short schematic network, evaluation comparison. Do not turn everything into icon cards. At most one decorative icon in any group; same semantic roles uniformly include or omit icons. NO text at all: no title, no letters, no digits, no mathematical symbols, no pseudo text, no watermark. Reserve ample blank strips beside or above each object for later real-font labels, plus blank areas beside distinct arrow types. A clean academic full-width landscape background, readable at textbook size.
Scientific content: static learning has a data-production chain: environment law plus observation mechanism produce a training RECORD DISTRIBUTION through deterministic integration; sampling that distribution creates a batch of independent training records. A separate task/candidate configuration and that batch jointly enter objective-and-feasible-set construction, then optimization produces ONE fixed learned candidate. A separate specified test record distribution produces an independent test batch. Both the fixed learned candidate and test batch feed ONE sample risk estimate. Exactly these nine semantic objects, every required dependency visibly connected. Keep training and testing separated; NEVER draw an arrow from test data or evaluation back to objective/optimization. Test distribution need not match training distribution, so show separate distribution objects. Integration must visibly differ from stochastic sampling, such as a kernel-like distribution operator and sample-sheet fan, but never draw quantitative data curves with claimed exact values. Retain a rich mechanism depiction within learning construction, not just identical rectangles. The learned candidate is a schematic network/function output with no invented architecture claim. No extra deployment nodes are necessary. Labels will later read: environment/observation μ,K; training law P_tr=μK; batch D~P_tr^n; configuration ℓ,C,H,Φ; objective F_D/feasible set; construction B; optimization; candidate h_D^(k)=A^(k)(D,U); test law P_te; independent test batch D_te~P_te^m; risk estimate. Do NOT draw these strings, only blank label areas. External ref1 shows separation of training and final evaluation; ref2 shows training inputs/learning vs fixed model inference. Use their mechanisms, not layout.
